name: CDNA3 Matrix Core MFMA instruction precision support (native vs emulated)
workarounds: TF32 is natively supported on CDNA3 (653.7 TFLOPS dense) but NOT on CDNA4 - CDNA4 emulates TF32 in software
FP8 (E4M3/E5M2) is natively supported on CDNA3 at 2614.9 TFLOPS dense
BF16 and FP16 share the same matrix core path at 1307.4 TFLOPS dense on CDNA3
INT8 shares the FP8 matrix core path at 2614.9 TFLOPS dense on CDNA3
notes: CDNA3 (gfx942) Matrix Cores natively execute: FP64 (256 FLOPS/clock/CU), FP32 (256), TF32 (1024 vector, no native matrix TF32 - the 653.7 TFLOPS figure is vector), FP16 (2048), BF16 (2048), FP8 (4096), INT8 (4096). The MFMA (Matrix Fused Multiply-Add) instruction is the hardware primitive. FP8 is 2x the FP16 rate. INT8 shares the FP8 path. CDNA3 does NOT support FP4 or FP6 natively - those are CDNA4 additions. TF32 on CDNA3 is listed as 'Vector TF32' at 1024 FLOPS/clock/CU, not a matrix path - the 653.7 TFLOPS peak is achieved through the vector units, not matrix cores. This is a key distinction: TF32 GEMMs on CDNA3 run on vector ALUs, not matrix cores.
